title: Three Leaders, One First: Trump, Xi and Putin Meet
summary:
For the first time, the leaders of the United States, China and Russia met formally. President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and the three countries released a joint statement.

The statement promised to release more oil and, for the first time, to hold formal talks about nuclear weapons. The US, Russia and China are the world's three biggest nuclear powers. The meeting lasted over 80 minutes.

President Trump said the meeting went great. President Putin called it the beginning of a new era of global diplomacy. But the countries still have deep divisions, and the statement is light on specifics.

The declaration also criticized the International Criminal Court. The US is trying to weaken the court, while the court is trying to arrest Putin over war crimes in Ukraine. The leaders agreed to plan talks to reduce nuclear risks.

Not everyone was cheering. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, 'Mr. Putin is not our friend, nor will he ever be.' The world will watch what the promises turn into.
why_it_matters: When the world's biggest nuclear powers talk to each other, it can help keep the world safer.
